conviction_note: The whole print turns on whether the FY26 guide ($7,800-7,900M sales / $950-980M adj EBITDA) survives, and the market is positioned for the Sept-2025 repeat (9.2% implied vs 4.48% median, +3.24 put skew, new 52-week low on 3 Sep, two August downgrades); but the BLS producer price index for the exact product CNM sells inflected inside the quarter and turned y/y-positive in July, which removes the larger of the two drivers of that 2025 cut, so I take roughly a third of the implied move to the upside and no more, because residential is genuinely worse and the option chain is too illiquid to lean on.

findings.finding: BLS PPI for 'Plastics Sewer, Stormdrain and Water Main Pipe' (WPU072106038) — CNM's single largest product exposure — averaged 185.2 across May/Jun/Jul 2026 (CNM's fiscal Q2, 4 May-2 Aug) versus 186.5 a year earlier, i.e. -0.7% y/y, against -8.2% y/y in CNM's fiscal Q1 (Feb-Apr 2026: 174.95 vs 190.48); the July 2026 reading of 188.565 is actually +1.9% ABOVE July 2025 and +8.2% above the March 2026 trough, so the deflation that drove the Sept-2025 guidance cut had fully reversed by the last month of this quarter.
findings.source_date: 2026-07-01 (latest monthly observation; series pulled 2026-09-08 via fredgraph.csv?id=WPU072106038)
findings.why_not_priced: On 10 June management told investors the opposite shape: Robyn Bradbury said 'PVC will still be down year over year even if we do get some uplift' and put the majority of the pricing impact in Q3, and the sell-side preview narrative into tomorrow is still PVC deflation. Nobody re-cuts a BLS six-digit commodity index onto a 4-May-to-2-August fiscal quarter. If the market had done it, CNM would not have printed a new 52-week low at $41.87 on 3 September, 25-delta puts would not be bid 3.24 vol points over calls, and Northcoast would not have cut to neutral on 26 August. The mechanism matters twice: it lifts Q2 revenue mix and, more importantly, it underwrites the 'low to mid single digit growth in Q3 and Q4' management needs to hold the FY guide (H2 FY25 was $3,643M; the guide implies $3,750-3,850M, i.e. +2.9% to +5.8%).
findings.independence: Two independent, non-BLS confirmations. (1) A waterworks distributor's own customer notice: United Pipe & Steel posted a new PVC pipe list price sheet dated 5/15 stating 'PVC pipe mills have announced a list price increase' on energy/raw-material costs — https://unitedpipe.com/blog/pvc-pipe-increase-new-list-price-sheet/ (2026-05-15), which lands in week two of CNM's quarter and explains the May PPI step. (2) Plumbing & Mechanical's trade-press tally of manufacturer increases inside and after the quarter: A.Y. McDonald +6-15% eff. 7 July (https://www.pmmag.com/articles/107578-phcp-pvf-price-increases-july-2026, 2026-07-08) and American Tube & Pipe +8%, Wheatland +8%, Matco Norca +4-11%, Legend Valve +3-25% eff. August (https://www.pmmag.com/articles/107644-phcp-pvf-price-increases-august-2026, 2026-08-06). A same-publisher corroborant that should be collapsed into this cluster, not counted separately: BLS ductile iron pressure pipe PPI (WPU10150211) rose from 464.775 in Apr/May 2026 to 476.788 in Jun/Jul, +7.2% since Dec 2025 — https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/WPU10150211.
findings._note: double-count guard: the ductile-iron series and the plastics-pipe-manufacturing series (PCU326122326122, 431.664 Apr -> 453.458 May -> 456.804 Jul) are the same BLS document family as the headline number and are listed as corroboration, not as separate findings.

findings.finding: Mueller Water Products — the largest US maker of fire hydrants and iron gate valves, sold almost entirely through waterworks distributors of which CNM is the biggest — reported its quarter ended 30 June 2026 (two of CNM's three Q2 months) on 5 August with net sales +4.1% to $395.9M driven 'primarily by higher pricing across most product lines' partially offset by slightly lower volumes, record adjusted EBITDA +24.3%, adjusted EPS +47.1%, and a third consecutive raise to FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance (to $367-372M).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a sell-through read on the 44% of CNM's net sales that is municipal, published 34 days before CNM's print — and CNM's tape did the opposite of absorbing it, making a fresh 52-week low at $41.87 on 3 September, four weeks after MWA raised. If the read had been transferred, the run-up would not be -5.1% over 20 days and the put skew would not be positive. The specific shape MWA reported (price up, volume slightly down, margin sharply up) is exactly the distributor-favourable mix, because a distributor holding pre-increase inventory books the spread; CNM guided gross margin only to 'remain at similar levels' to Q1's 27.2%.
findings.independence: CNM's own Q1 10-Q gives the end-market split that makes the read load-bearing (~44% municipal, 38% non-residential, 18% residential for FY ended 1 Feb 2026): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001856525/000185652526000054/cnm-20260503.htm (2026-06-10). Separately, Westlake's Q2 2026 release describes 'higher end market demand for pipe and fittings' sequentially in HIP while its PEM segment EBITDA went $36M to $416M on higher PVC resin pricing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1262823/000126282326000026/ex991_20260630earningsrele.htm (2026-08-04).

findings.finding: US single-family housing starts fell 9.9% m/m in July 2026 to an 808k SAAR, the lowest since November 2022 — a deterioration inside the final month of CNM's quarter and after management said on 10 June that residential lot development had 'largely stabilized' with 'no further deterioration'.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly it is priced — housing weakness is the consensus bear case on CNM and is the obvious reason for the -35% twelve-month decline, the two August downgrades and the bid for downside. The residual that is not priced is narrow and specific: it invalidates the exact word management used on the last call ('stabilized'), so the risk is a verbal walk-back on the lot-development commentary rather than a numbers surprise. I size it small deliberately, and it is the reason my net number is a third of the implied move rather than half.
findings.independence: Same underlying Census release read by a second outlet: https://www.housingwire.com/articles/july-2026-housing-starts-drop-permits-rise/ — treat as one source, not two. Cutting the other way, residential is only ~18% of CNM net sales per the Q1 10-Q cited above.

findings.finding: CNM raised $750M of 6.000% senior notes due 2034 on 1 July 2026 — inside fiscal Q2 — with proceeds earmarked for prepaying the 2028 term loan and for 'general corporate purposes, including... mergers and acquisitions, share repurchases', at the same time as it had $581M left on the $1bn authorisation, had just run its highest-ever quarterly buyback ($88M / 1.8M shares in Q1 plus $37M / 0.8M shares in the five weeks to 10 June), and management flagged 'a pretty notable uptick in the pipeline... to larger opportunities' and said it might 'overperform some of our M&A goals'.
findings.why_not_priced: The financing itself is wire copy; what is not is the combination — fresh unsecured capacity plus an untouched $1,226M ABL plus net debt down to $2,010M plus a stock that spent the back half of the quarter falling from ~$46 to a 52-week low. If a materially larger Q2 repurchase, an authorisation increase, or a sizeable acquisition were expected with the print, the stock would not be trading 4.4% off its 52-week low with an option chain whose ATM bid-ask is 72% of mid — that spread is itself evidence nobody is positioned for a capital-return catalyst. The 1 July closing also puts a loss on debt extinguishment into reported GAAP EPS but not adjusted EPS, a small headline-versus-consensus trap at the open.
findings.independence: The buyback pace and remaining authorisation come from a different document, the Q1 press release and 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1856525/000185652526000053/cnmq12026earningspressrele.htm (2026-06-10). The M&A pipeline quotes come from the Q1 call transcript: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/10/core-and-main-cnm-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/ (2026-06-10) — note that transcript is also the source of the PVC quote in finding 1, so the two share one document and should be collapsed on that dimension.

searched_and_found_nothing: Event reality: already sealed as confirmed; company PR confirms 9 Sep 2026 bmo with an 08:30 ET call, and no re-check was needed.

An unannounced large acquisition: the June/July 8-K exhibits are only the notes indenture, supplemental indenture and the Sixth Amendment $800M term loan (SOFR+175, due 2033) — no acquisition agreement, and no credible deal rumour found.

PVC pipe antitrust: CNM is named as an alleged co-conspirator, not a defendant, in In re PVC Pipe Antitrust Litigation, and I found no 2026 development that reaches CNM; the Q1 10-Q shows no material change to legal proceedings.

coreandmain.com and ir.coreandmain.com both return HTTP 403 to the fetcher, so I could not read the news archive, greenfield-opening cadence or any post-June tuck-in announcements directly from the company.

plasticstoday.com and plasticsnews.com resin-pricing pages return HTTP 403; I could not verify whether North American PVC resin rolled over in August 2026, which is the main unresolved risk to finding 1 (it would not change the quarter, which is closed and covered by the July PPI, but it would weaken the H2 guidance case). Search snippets on this were undated and I refused to use them.
Hiring signal: only aggregate open-role counts (209 on Glassdoor, 191 on Indeed) with no historical baseline — unusable as a trend.

Form 4 cluster: 13 Form 4s since 1 June (eight on 24 June, then 8 Jul, 23 Jul, 5 Aug) but EDGAR's list view would not resolve reporting owners for me, so I could not test for an insider buy at the lows; Form 144s on 27 May, 29 May and 30 June are sales and look routine.
No August or September 8-K, no pre-announcement, no guidance update, and no company statement of any kind between 2 July and the print.

The 'only two estimates' anomaly in the sweep row: the $0.919 EPS / $2.136Bn revenue consensus reconciles with broad coverage and management's own 'slight growth in the second quarter' framing — it is not a two-model artefact and there is no edge in it.
baseline_tension: It cuts against the baseline on every axis — the skew pays for downside, the 20-day run-up is -5.1%, the stock printed a 52-week low five sessions ago and the implied move is double this name's own history, all of which prices a repeat of the September-2025 guidance cut, while the producer price data for CNM's exact product and its largest supplier's overlapping quarter both say the deflation that caused that cut reversed inside this one.
